title: Lesson 7
paragraph: プロジェクトと業務管理

words.meaning: an important point or achievement used to track a project's progress
words.japaneseMeaning: 重要な節目・マイルストーン
words.example: Completing the first trial is a major milestone.

words.meaning: the agreed range of work and outcomes included in a project
words.example: The team agreed on the scope before estimating the cost.

words.meaning: a plan showing when tasks or events will happen
words.example: The schedule shows when each stage should begin.

words.meaning: a limit or condition that restricts what a project can do
words.example: The small budget is an important constraint.

words.meaning: a relationship in which one task relies on another task or resource
words.example: The schedule shows a dependency between design approval and production.

words.meaning: a prepared alternative course of action for a possible problem
words.japaneseMeaning: 不測の事態に備えた計画
words.example: The team prepared a contingency plan for delivery delays.

sentencePractice.prompt: The team prepares an alternative way to deliver the order if the main supplier fails. This is a ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: An alternative course prepared for a possible problem is a contingency plan; an order and a financial position statement do not serve that purpose.

words.meaning: a stage or resource that limits the flow or speed of an entire process
words.japaneseMeaning: ボトルネック・作業の詰まり
words.example: The single packing machine became a bottleneck.

words.meaning: the maximum amount of work or output a system can handle under stated conditions
words.example: The factory is operating close to full capacity.

words.meaning: the goods and materials a business holds for sale or use
words.example: The warehouse checks inventory at the end of each week.

sentencePractice.prompt: The warehouse record lists the goods and materials the business currently holds. It records the ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Goods and materials held by the business are inventory; wage records and timing plans are different records.

words.meaning: planned activities that give confidence a process will meet quality requirements
words.example: Quality assurance includes documented procedures and regular process reviews.
